audit_2026_10_18: Source audit (live CKAN datastore, 2026-10-18): dataset `building-permits` ('Building Permits') on data.sanantonio.gov, publisher City of San Antonio (Development Services; catalog organization 'Land and Building Development'), license Creative Commons Attribution (cc-by). Four resources; the connector uses PERMITS ISSUED (c21106f9-3ef5-4f3a-8604-f992b4db7512, datastore-active) — the archive resource covers 2020-2024 and APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED is applications, not issuances. PERMITS ISSUED: 150,205 rows, DATE ISSUED 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-16; resource last_modified 2026-10-18T04:01:29Z (the city reloads the file daily, ~04:00Z); the freshest DATE ISSUED inside it is 2026-10-16 — a measured TWO-DAY issuance lag (the Phase-1 plan claimed 2-4 days; measured at the short end, 2026-10-18). Freshness for this feed is measured as the resource's own last_modified stamp from package_show; the 96h threshold absorbs the daily reload plus the issuance lag with room. IDENTITY (trailing-12-month window, "DATE ISSUED" >= '2025-10-17'): 80,965 rows = 71,761 distinct PERMIT # (68,662 permits x 1 row; 3,099 permit numbers fan out to 2-126 rows). Across all 3,099 multi-row groups the rows NEVER disagree on ADDRESS, DATE ISSUED, or WORK TYPE (0 groups each, measured NULL-sensitively on a full audit pull); PERMIT TYPE varies inside 2,054 groups (component rows: one issuance whose rows name its component permit types — e.g. a remodel permit and its electrical component sharing one number, address, and issue date) and DATE SUBMITTED varies inside 1,053 groups (repeat submission/amendment rows under the same issuance). Rule: one published permit = one PERMIT #, collapsed in the pipeline (registry collapse_events); the pull order (issue date, permit #, submitted date) makes the representative row the permit's earliest submission. SCOPE (the plan's 'noisy permit types - filter needed', made exact): the register also issues NON-CONSTRUCTION permits — Garage Sale 3,679 permits, Tree Affidavit Permit 2,908, Across the Street Banner 424, Temporary Weekend Sign 96, Feather Sign 71, Avenue Sign 34, Event Sign 10, Inflatable Sign 4. Measured: those types NEVER mix with construction types under one permit number (0 mixed permits), so the scope filter is exact at either grain: 7,226 of 71,761 window permits (10.1%) are non-construction-only and are excluded by pull_where_extra; scoped window = 73,739 rows = 64,535 permits (verified identically by a source-side SQL count and the full audit pull). KEPT deliberately: Tree Permit (550; authorizes tree work on a site), Pedestrian Protection Permit (5; construction protection), Building Move Permit (23), Maintenance Permit (418) — families authorizing physical work. VALUATION (DECLARED VALUATION, a text float): populated on only 1,834 of 80,965 window rows; at permit level 1,833 of 71,761 permits (2.55%) state any figure — 54 at $0, 3 at $1 — and coverage is essentially the commercial building core (Comm New Building 572/572 rows, Comm Finish Out 144/144, Comm Shell 51/51, Comm Sitework 404/478, Comm Fence 176/177) while residential and trade permits state nothing. Within multi-row groups only ONE permit states two distinct figures ($27.7M / $33M, an amended sitework figure; the record stores the larger). The stamp disease is present inside the valued slice: whole-project values repeat across a project's separate permits ($114,115,277 x17 permits, $51,580,699 x37, $39,840,180 x31, $37,375,000 x35, $66,621,051 x22, $36,699,990 x26, $34,963,000 x24; the $365,806,696 project appears on both its drive and building permits). A scoped total under the store-the-stated-figure rule would read $16,828,385,879 built from 2.8% of permits with project values multiply counted — no honest county total exists, so values are stored as reported and NEVER published (counts-only). CROSS-CHECK targets (scoped, source-side): September 2026 = 5,398 permits (raw register 6,300); October 2026 to the 16th = 2,886 (raw 3,466). Scoped monthly (permits): 2025-10: 2,796 (from Oct 17) / 2025-11: 4,734 / 2025-12: 4,372 / 2026-01: 4,766 / 2026-02: 5,074 / 2026-03: 5,847 / 2026-04: 5,729 / 2026-05: 5,280 / 2026-06: 5,949 / 2026-07: 6,057 / 2026-08: 5,647 / 2026-09: 5,398 / 2026-10: 2,886. ADDRESS: one free-text field, canonical form 'STREET, City of San Antonio, TX ZIP' on 71,156 of 80,965 rows; variants include 'City of San Antonio ETJ' and enclave cities (Hollywood Park); 78,252 rows carry a 5-digit ZIP. PRIVACY: the register's only name-bearing fields are PRIMARY CONTACT (person names — individual applicants; sampled: a garage-sale applicant's name) and PROJECT NAME (mixes applicant person names with project labels); there is NO contractor/business field. Both name fields are excluded from pull_select entirely. NOTE: the CKAN SQL endpoint forbids some SQL (FILTER clauses, scalar subqueries); plain aggregates, GROUP BY, JOIN-free subqueries in FROM, and NOT IN lists all work. The endpoint did not throttle during the audit at 1s pacing.
coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of San Antonio (Development Services Department) only. Bexar County's other municipalities publish their permits separately and are not in this feed; the city's permitting jurisdiction (including its extraterritorial jurisdiction) is what the feed covers.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one PERMIT # in the PERMITS ISSUED register — one issuance by the City of San Antonio Development Services Department. The register's grain is one row per permit-type component an issuance covers, plus repeat submission rows for amended applications: a remodel permit and its electrical component share one permit number, one address, and one issue date, as do a sitework permit's many submission rows. The pipeline collapses each permit's rows into one record (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the representative row is the permit's earliest submission (pull order: issue date, permit number, submitted date).
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window ("DATE ISSUED" >= '2025-10-17'), measured 2026-10-18 on a full audit pull verified against source-side counts (80,965 rows both ways): 80,965 rows = 71,761 distinct PERMIT #; 3,099 permit numbers fan out to 2-126 rows. Across all multi-row permits the rows disagree on NONE of ADDRESS, DATE ISSUED, or WORK TYPE (NULL-sensitive, 0 groups each; re-asserted by the pipeline's collapse step on the production pull). PERMIT TYPE varies in 2,054 groups and DATE SUBMITTED in 1,053 — the component and submission shapes the rule describes. After the registry's scope filter (see field_map.scope_rule), the published window is 73,739 rows = 64,535 permits.
dedupe_rule.rule: source_record_id = PERMIT #. Collapse happens in the pipeline (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the in-batch duplicate gate and the DB upsert key remain as guards.

field_map.application_date: DATE SUBMITTED of the permit's earliest-submitted row (the collapse representative). Every window permit carries one; only 2 permits' earliest submission postdates their issue date (source noise, mirrored as reported)
field_map.category: NOT PUBLISHED — the register's type names mix Res/Comm prefixes inconsistently across families and the trade families are unmarked, so no consistent residential/commercial class exists; category stays NULL (the Boston honest-NULL treatment)
field_map.contractor_rule: NONE CARRIED — the register publishes no contractor or business field at all. Its two name-bearing fields are PRIMARY CONTACT (person names, verified on sampled rows) and PROJECT NAME (applicant names mixed with project labels); both are excluded from the pull's column list entirely and never requested. contractor_name stays NULL, never inferred (the Boston treatment).
field_map.issue_date: "DATE ISSUED" (a TEXT column of plain ISO dates; every register row carries one — the publisher includes issued permits only). The window field; see ckan_window_field_sql
field_map.permit_type: the collapsed permit's PERMIT TYPE set, joined with '; ' (the Cincinnati treatment — the set names the issuance's component families)
field_map.project_description: NOT PUBLISHED — the register publishes no scope-of-work text (PROJECT NAME is a name-bearing field and is never requested), so project_description stays NULL, never invented
field_map.scope_rule: pull_where_extra excludes the register's non-construction families at pull time: Garage Sale, Tree Affidavit Permit, Across the Street Banner, Temporary Weekend Sign, Feather Sign, Inflatable Sign, Event Sign, Avenue Sign — permits authorizing a sale, an affidavit filing, or a temporary display, never construction. Measured exactness: those types never share a permit number with a construction type (0 mixed permits in the window), so 7,226 non-construction permits are excluded and every construction permit is kept whole. The exclusion is named and counted on the Data Sources page. Gate 4's expected count is computed on the identical where, so the baseline compares like with like (the San Francisco precedent).
field_map.status_source: the register publishes NO status field; it is a permits-issued register, so status is 'issued' by the register's own definition and status_source stays NULL (the Baton Rouge treatment)
field_map.valuation: DECLARED VALUATION — stored as reported (the collapsed permit's stated figure; where a permit's rows restate one figure it is stored once; the one window permit stating two figures, $27.7M then $33M, stores the larger, its amended figure) but NEVER PUBLISHED: Bexar County runs counts-only. Evidence (registry audit): the field is populated on only 2.55% of window permits — essentially the commercial building core — and inside that slice it restates whole-project values across a project's separate permits ($114,115,277 on 17 permits; $51,580,699 on 37), the Seattle stamp disease; a county total would be built from a fortieth of the permits with project values multiply counted. No trustworthy aggregate exists (contrast Boston, where the field was 100% populated and verified to the cent).
field_map.work_type_source: PERMIT TYPE set — dedicated classifier pass: trades.classify_sa_trade (WORK TYPE is NULL on 65,626 of 80,965 rows and names only New/Existing/Other; it is an agreement field of the collapse, not a classification signal)

license: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) — the license named in the dataset's data.sanantonio.gov catalog record; figures attributed to the City of San Antonio
order_tiebreak: "PERMIT #", "DATE SUBMITTED" (see order_sql — the full quoted fragment the pipeline uses)
pull_where_extra: "PERMIT TYPE" NOT IN ('Garage Sale', 'Tree Affidavit Permit', 'Across the Street Banner', 'Temporary Weekend Sign', 'Feather Sign', 'Inflatable Sign', 'Event Sign', 'Avenue Sign')
rate_limit: CKAN datastore SQL API, 5,000-row pages with the adapter's 1.0s pacing plus hard-backoff retries (Boston precedent — the endpoint family throttles bursts; San Antonio's endpoint served the paced audit and pull steadily). The SQL dialect forbids FILTER clauses and scalar subqueries.
source_name: City of San Antonio open data (San Antonio Open Data) — Building Permits, permits issued
terms_status: verified-open-2026-10-18: the data.sanantonio.gov catalog record for `building-permits` (publisher: City of San Antonio) names the Creative Commons Attribution license (CC BY) — reuse permitted with attribution; accessLevel public. Figures are published 'as reported by the City of San Antonio' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: daily file reload (resource last_modified 2026-10-18T04:01:29Z on audit day) with a measured two-day issuance lag: the freshest DATE ISSUED in the file on 2026-10-18 is 2026-10-16. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the datastore resource's last_modified stamp from package_show (the CKAN equivalent of the source's own dataset stamp); the 96h threshold covers the daily reload cadence.
watermark_field: "DATE ISSUED" + "PERMIT #" (issue-date window; per-component/submission rows collapse to permits by PERMIT # — see dedupe_rule)
